about: The ground surfaces' mechanics as the drone's parts meet them (p7a-ground design 1; PHY-01, D-021, D-024): for each of the thirteen surfaces S01–S13, in MapWorld.SurfaceIds' and lib/meta.SURFACE_IDS' order, a dry, a wet and a saturated set (Sunny reads dry, Rain wet, Severe rain saturated), and for each kind the world's drawn elements are made of (straw, stem, twig, leaf) a dry and a wet set (Rain and Severe rain both read wet). The soil is Bekker's linear pressure–sinkage, p = (k_c/b + k_phi)·z (n = 1), under Wong's load and unload rule. The relief, the pitfalls and the elements themselves are the world's (map data and asset records), never this table's, and nothing about the ground is drawn: an element's value inside a [min, max] range comes from its own Id's hash. K§7.2's mats (meadow thatch, leaf litter, ash) are not here: no such ground is on the test range (D-047), and a straw layer is a shape of physics_materials.json's straw. Physics-owned: values change here with physics sign-off; the log records the rows and the file's hash, and a replay refuses a log flown with another file. Every number is labelled where it stands (pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed) with its source or reason; a value labelled derived meets its formula ('fields') or the loader refuses the file; the wet and saturated sets start from the dry set by the named factors of 'wetting', and a value that departs from them is labelled with its own reason.

fields.labelled number: {"value": <a number, or [min, max], a range an element draws from by its own Id's hash>, "label": "pilot" | "measured" | "published" | "derived" | "assumed", "note": "<source, reason or formula>"}; the note is required
fields.constants.reference_width_m: b_ref, Bekker's width b at which bearing_n_per_m3 is stated: the K§7.2 reference foot's. b is the smaller dimension of a contact (a rectangle's width, a circle's radius), so a half-skid's is its groove's chord and a sphere's its footprint's radius
fields.constants.firm_layer_n_per_m3: the firm layer past max_sink_m: it adds this modulus × the footprint × the sink past max_sink_m
fields.wetting: the named factors and values the wet and saturated sets are derived by: a soil's bearing, unload ratio, maximum sink and both frictions × wetting.<name>_<level>, its cohesive share, damping and lip as the dry set's, its adhesions and release as wetting's values; a rigid surface's frictions × the friction factor; a cover kind's hook release × cover_hook_release_wet, straw's modulus, cut energy and density × their factors, a leaf's fresh mass per area + leaf_water_film_kg_m2, and the rest as the dry set's
fields.surfaces.<id>.<set>: a soil set holds every field below; a rigid set (asphalt, a concrete slab) holds only friction_static and friction_kinetic, and the part's own spring carries it
fields.bearing_n_per_m3: the virgin-loading modulus at b_ref, k_c/b_ref + k_phi (N/m³; K§7.2's bearing)
fields.cohesive_share: the share of bearing_n_per_m3 that is k_c/b_ref, the part that falls as a contact widens
fields.k_c_n_per_m2: Bekker's cohesive modulus (n = 1): cohesive_share × bearing_n_per_m3 × reference_width_m
fields.unload_ratio: Wong's unload and reload stiffness over the virgin loading's, over the groove's footprint at its deepest sink (at least 1; 1 is elastic)
fields.max_sink_m: the sink past which the firm layer adds its modulus
fields.damping_ns_per_m3: viscous damping per footprint area: the force is this × the footprint × the sink's rate
fields.friction_static: μs of the drone's polymer and carbon parts on the surface; a part's anchor holds to μs·Fn + interface_adhesion_pa·S + the groove's passive resistance
fields.friction_kinetic: μk, the same pairing; the anchor slides at μk·Fn plus the same two
fields.adhesion_pa: σ_a: the normal pull per wetted footprint on a part that has loaded the soil, as it lifts, falling linearly to nothing at adhesion_release_m from the groove's set (a cohesive zone); 0 when dry
fields.interface_adhesion_pa: c_a: the shear adhesion per wetted footprint added to the anchor's limits (τ = c_a + σ·tan δ); 0 when dry
fields.adhesion_release_m: δ_a: the separation at which the adhesion lets go; above 0 wherever adhesion_pa is
fields.lip_edge_radius_m: the radius the fiber bends over at a groove's or a cut's lip (p7d-tether)
fields.cover.<kind>: straw, stem and twig hold elastic_modulus_pa, wall_share, density_kg_m3, hook_release_n, cut_energy_j_per_m2 and damping_ratio, and straw and twig roll_friction; a leaf holds its masses, petiole_diameter_m and cut_energy_j_per_m2
fields.wall_share: the hollow wall's thickness over the diameter; 0.5 is a solid section
fields.density_kg_m3: the wall tissue's density: the mass a blade brings to its speed is this × the section × one chord
fields.hook_release_n: [min, max]: the pull at which a hooked element lets go (it slips off, pulls out or breaks)
fields.cut_energy_j_per_m2: e_s: the energy per section area to cut through it (a leaf's at its petiole)
fields.roll_friction: μ across a loose element's axis as it rolls under a part
fields.dry_mass_per_area_kg_m2: a leaf's dry mass per area (LMA)
fields.dry_matter_content: a leaf's dry mass over its fresh mass
fields.mass_per_area_kg_m2: a leaf's fresh mass per area: dry_mass_per_area_kg_m2 / dry_matter_content; wet, plus the film
fields.petiole_diameter_m: a leaf's stalk, where its cut is taken

reference_width_m.label: derived
reference_width_m.note: the K§7.2 reference foot is a flat 15 mm disc (surfaces-review §1–§2); Bekker's b is the smaller dimension of a contact, a rectangle's width or a circular plate's radius (Bekker 1969; Wong 2008, the published convention), so b_ref = 0.015 m / 2; p7a-ground design 1 wrote 0.015 m (the diameter), and the published convention is kept here

firm_layer_n_per_m3.label: assumed
firm_layer_n_per_m3.note: carried (K§7.1 step 3, surfaces-review §1): the firm subsoil a sink past max_sink_m meets

bearing_wet.label: assumed
bearing_wet.note: the published order: Wong 2008 tabulates loams and clays whose Bekker moduli fall severalfold to more than tenfold between a drier and a wetter state; 0.3 assumed for ground wetted by rain from above

bearing_saturated.label: assumed
bearing_saturated.note: half the wet factor again for ground at saturation (assumed), toward the wettest tabulated states' order of magnitude (Wong 2008)

unload_ratio_wet.label: assumed
unload_ratio_wet.note: a wetter soil is more plastic and keeps more of its sink as set (assumed; the published direction: a loam's plastic range is crossed as it wets)

unload_ratio_saturated.label: assumed
unload_ratio_saturated.note: as unload_ratio_wet (assumed, p7a-ground design 1); a named factor of its own so the two can be tuned apart

max_sink_wet.label: assumed
max_sink_wet.note: a wetted top layer stays soft to a greater depth before the firm subsoil (assumed)

max_sink_saturated.label: assumed
max_sink_saturated.note: as max_sink_wet (assumed, p7a-ground design 1); a named factor of its own

friction_wet.label: assumed
friction_wet.note: soil on a smooth part passes from friction to adhesion to lubrication as its moisture rises (Nichols 1931, the published phases): the friction coefficient falls as a film forms while the interface adhesion takes over; 0.8 assumed

friction_saturated.label: assumed
friction_saturated.note: past the sticky point the film lubricates (Nichols 1931's third phase); 0.6 assumed

adhesion_wet_pa.label: assumed
adhesion_wet_pa.note: soil's normal adhesion to a part is of the order of kPa (Fountaine 1954, the published order); 3 kPa assumed: a corner's half-skid with a 2.2e-3 m² wetted footprint (z ≥ r) is held by 6.6 N as it lifts, of the order of its 12.7 N share of 5.18 kg (derived)

adhesion_saturated_pa.label: assumed
adhesion_saturated_pa.note: an object lifted from a saturated bed meets breakout suction as well (Vesic 1971; Foda 1982, published); 5 kPa assumed: 11 N on a 2.2e-3 m² footprint (derived)

interface_adhesion_wet_pa.label: assumed
interface_adhesion_wet_pa.note: the shear adhesion on a smooth part, c_a = α·c, with Tomlinson 1957's adhesion factor α of 0.5–1 for soft clays (published) and a wet loam's cohesion of a few kPa (Wong 2008's wetter states); 2 kPa assumed

interface_adhesion_saturated_pa.label: assumed
interface_adhesion_saturated_pa.note: past the sticky point the film lubricates the shear (Nichols 1931's third phase) while the normal suction grows; 1 kPa assumed

adhesion_release_wet_m.label: assumed
adhesion_release_wet_m.note: the separation at which the film parts (a cohesive zone, Dugdale 1960, Barenblatt 1962): 2 mm assumed, so the work to part is ½·σ_a·δ_a·S, 6.6 mJ on 2.2e-3 m² (derived)

adhesion_release_saturated_m.label: assumed
adhesion_release_saturated_m.note: 3 mm assumed for the deeper, wetter groove: 16.5 mJ on 2.2e-3 m² (derived)

cover_hook_release_wet.label: assumed
cover_hook_release_wet.note: a wet element clings to a part and holds harder before it slips off (assumed, p7a-ground design 1)

straw_modulus_wet.label: assumed
straw_modulus_wet.note: dead straw softens as it takes up water: its Young's modulus falls with moisture content (Tavakoli et al. 2009, the published direction); 0.7 assumed. Live stems and twigs are already at full turgor, and rain wets only their surface, so they keep their dry modulus (assumed)

straw_cut_energy_wet.label: assumed
straw_cut_energy_wet.note: wetter straw is tougher to shear: its shear strength and specific shearing energy rise with moisture (Tavakoli et al. 2009, the published direction); 1.5 assumed; live tissue keeps its dry value (assumed)

straw_density_wet.label: assumed
straw_density_wet.note: dead straw takes up rain: from about 10 % to about 40 % moisture on a dry basis (assumed) its mass rises 1.4/1.1 = 1.27 (derived), so 1.3

leaf_water_film_kg_m2.label: assumed
leaf_water_film_kg_m2.note: a wet leaf carries a film of water: canopy interception storage is of the order of 0.1–0.3 mm per unit leaf area (the published order of forest interception studies), so 0.2 mm, 0.2 kg/m² of leaf (assumed)

bearing_n_per_m3.label: assumed
bearing_n_per_m3.note: carried (K§7.2; surfaces-review §1–§4): the 15 mm reference foot at 25 N sinks 25/(bearing·π·0.0075²) = 20.2 mm (derived), K§7.2's 20 mm

cohesive_share.label: assumed
cohesive_share.note: a root-bound loam; Wong 2008's tabulated soils put k_c/b at a 7.5 mm plate near k_phi for loams and clays and far below it for dry sand (the published order)

damping_ns_per_m3.label: assumed
damping_ns_per_m3.note: carried (K§7.2; surfaces-review §1–§4); surfaces-review §4 expects the soft soils' to fall in tuning, where it overlaps their plastic loss

friction_static.label: assumed
friction_static.note: carried (K§7.2; surfaces-review §1–§4); the drone's smooth carbon skids on soil: Potyondy 1961's interface ratios δ/φ of 0.5–0.9 for smooth to rough construction materials, at φ 30–40°, give tan δ ≈ 0.3–0.7 (derived)

adhesion_pa.note: dry: no water film, Nichols 1931's friction phase

dirt_track.about: S13: a wheel-compacted silt loam track, its ruts the zone's relief (map data)

bearing_n_per_m3.label: assumed
bearing_n_per_m3.note: new (p7a-ground design 1): a dry, wheel-compacted silt loam marks under the 15 mm reference foot's 25 N (141 kPa) by about 1 mm, its loose dust and crumb (assumed); the compacted body beneath, of the order of E 20–50 MPa (the published order for compacted silts and stiff clays), gives under 0.1 mm as an elastic punch, π·a·(1 − ν²)·q/(2E) (Boussinesq's rigid disc, derived); so bearing = 25 N/(π·0.0075²·1 mm) = 1.41e8 N/m³, rounded to 1.4e8 (1.01 mm, derived): the stiffest soil of the table, a skid on it is carried by its leg

cohesive_share.label: assumed
cohesive_share.note: a compacted silt loam; Wong 2008's tabulated soils put k_c/b at a 7.5 mm plate near k_phi for loams and clays and far below it for dry sand (the published order)

unload_ratio.label: assumed
unload_ratio.note: a compacted soil is nearly elastic, as dry_crust and rubble (K§7.2's 1.5)

max_sink_m.label: assumed
max_sink_m.note: the loose dust and crumb over the compacted body, past which the firm layer adds

damping_ns_per_m3.label: assumed
damping_ns_per_m3.note: dry_crust's (K§7.2), the nearest firm, dry row

friction_static.label: assumed
friction_static.note: a dusty compacted silt loam, as the K§7.2 loams' 0.6/0.5; the drone's smooth carbon skids on soil: Potyondy 1961's interface ratios δ/φ of 0.5–0.9 for smooth to rough construction materials, at φ 30–40°, give tan δ ≈ 0.3–0.7 (derived)

adhesion_pa.label: assumed
adhesion_pa.note: dry: no water film, Nichols 1931's friction phase

interface_adhesion_pa.label: assumed
interface_adhesion_pa.note: dry: no water film, Nichols 1931's friction phase

lip_edge_radius_m.label: assumed

elastic_modulus_pa.label: published
elastic_modulus_pa.note: wheat straw's Young's modulus, 4.8–6.6 GPa (O'Dogherty et al. 1995)

wall_share.label: assumed
wall_share.note: a wheat straw's wall is a few tenths of a millimetre on a 3–4 mm stem, about an eighth of the diameter

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: the dry wall tissue: a 3.5 mm straw with a 0.4 mm wall (3.9e-6 m² of wall) weighs about 2 g a metre (derived), the order of a dry wheat straw's mass for its length

cut_energy_j_per_m2.label: assumed
cut_energy_j_per_m2.note: the published order of straw and forage shearing, 10–60 kJ/m² of section (Persson 1987; Tavakoli et al. 2009 for wheat straw), dry straw toward its low end

roll_friction.label: assumed
roll_friction.note: carried (K§7.3): a loose straw or twig rolls under a part across its axis

damping_ratio.label: assumed
damping_ratio.note: p7a-ground design 8: a straw or stem bending as a cantilever

elastic_modulus_pa.label: assumed
elastic_modulus_pa.note: the solid-section moduli K§7.2's grass and straw stems imply, 0.5–4 GPa (surfaces-review §2 issue 5), within the order of herbaceous stems' (Niklas 1992)

wall_share.label: assumed
wall_share.note: many weed stems are hollow or pithy; the pith carries little, so a wall of a fifth of the diameter

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: green herbaceous tissue, mostly water with air spaces

cut_energy_j_per_m2.label: assumed
cut_energy_j_per_m2.note: a green, fibrous stalk: the published order of stalk shearing, 10–60 kJ/m² (Persson 1987), above dry straw

damping_ratio.label: assumed
damping_ratio.note: p7a-ground design 8: a rooted stem's bending

elastic_modulus_pa.label: published
elastic_modulus_pa.note: the green moduli of temperate hardwoods, about 7–13 GPa (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a; black locust 12.8); a young twig's juvenile wood, pith and bark sit toward the low end

wall_share.label: derived
wall_share.note: a twig is solid wood: the wall reaches its centre

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: green wood: the Wood Handbook's green-volume specific gravity of 0.4–0.66 for temperate hardwoods at a twig's green moisture of 50–100 % of its dry mass gives 600–1300 kg/m³ (ρ = G·(1 + MC)·1000, derived); 950 for a twig high in water

cut_energy_j_per_m2.label: assumed
cut_energy_j_per_m2.note: green wood cut across its grain by a blunt, fast edge: above stalks, the order of woody stems in Persson 1987

roll_friction.label: assumed
roll_friction.note: carried (K§7.3): a twig under a part is a rigid roller

damping_ratio.label: assumed
damping_ratio.note: p7a-ground design 8: a crown twig or a stem bending as a cantilever

dry_mass_per_area_kg_m2.label: assumed
dry_mass_per_area_kg_m2.note: Wright et al. 2004's leaf mass per area of temperate broadleaves, 30–120 g/m² (published); a thin leaflet toward the low side, 60 g/m²

dry_matter_content.label: assumed
dry_matter_content.note: the published order of temperate woody species' leaf dry-matter content, 0.2–0.4 g/g (e.g. Wilson et al. 1999)

mass_per_area_kg_m2.label: derived
mass_per_area_kg_m2.note: the fresh leaf: dry_mass_per_area_kg_m2 / dry_matter_content; a blade strikes the leaf with its water, so a 4 cm² leaflet is 0.08 g (p7a-ground design 8–9 took the dry 0.02 g)

petiole_diameter_m.label: assumed
petiole_diameter_m.note: a leaflet's stalk, where a blade cuts it free

cut_energy_j_per_m2.label: assumed
cut_energy_j_per_m2.note: the petiole, a green stalk, as stems
